headline: Secure Wisconsin State Park Vehicle Admission
reservation: A Wisconsin State Park vehicle admission sticker is required for entry and should be purchased online or at the park office. Campsite reservations are handled through the central state system and typically fill months in advance for summer weekends; verify current booking windows on the official DNR site.

days.title: Quartzite Bluffs and Overlooks

stops.name: East Bluff Trail
stops.detail: Climb the stone stairs to view the Devil's Doorway rock formation and panoramic lake vistas.

stops.name: Balanced Rock
stops.detail: Observe this precarious geological feature while navigating the steep descent toward the South Shore.

days.driving: Allow 20–30 minutes for park transit; parking areas fill early.
days.note: Quartzite steps can be slippery when wet; wear footwear with aggressive traction.

days.title: Shoreline Perspectives
days.start: Suggested: 9:30 AM from the North Shore

stops.name: Tumbled Rocks Trail
stops.detail: Walk the level path along the western shoreline beneath massive fallen boulders without the bluff climb.

stops.name: North Shore Beach
stops.detail: Utilize the beach and picnic areas for a relaxed afternoon by the clear glacial waters.

days.driving: Minimal driving; primarily walking between park facilities.
days.note: Check water quality advisories at the park office before swimming.

days.title: Baraboo Hills Heritage
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from the South Shore

stops.name: Circus World
stops.detail: Visit the National Historic Landmark site in Baraboo to learn about the region's circus history.

stops.name: International Crane Foundation
stops.detail: Explore the outdoor exhibits dedicated to the world's crane species in a nearby wooded setting.

days.driving: Allow 40–60 minutes for regional travel between sites; roads are two-lane rural routes.
days.note: Verify seasonal operating hours for museums, as they differ significantly from park hours.

intel.title: Peak Demand
intel.text: The North and South Shore lots often reach capacity by mid-morning on summer weekends. Arrive before 8 AM or consider visiting on a weekday to ensure access to your preferred trailhead.

intel.title: Bluff Coverage
intel.text: Cellular signal is generally reliable on the bluff tops but can be blocked by rock walls at the lake level. Carry a physical park map to navigate the intersecting trail systems accurately.

intel.title: Local Services
intel.text: Baraboo serves as the primary hub for fuel and groceries, located just minutes from the North Shore entrance. There are no retail fuel services within the park boundaries.

intel.title: Hiking Safety
intel.text: Allow at least three hours for a full bluff loop to avoid descending in fading light. High-traffic periods occur between 10 AM and 3 PM.

intel.title: Rental Equipment
intel.text: Kayak and canoe rentals are available seasonally at the North and South Shores; confirm current availability at the concession stands. Life jackets are required for all boaters.

plan.arrival: From MSN airport, it is roughly a 70-minute drive; stop in Sauk City or Baraboo for camp supplies before checking in at the park visitor center.
plan.vehicle: Passenger cars are suitable for all paved park roads; RVs should verify site lengths and overhang clearances at the specific campground loops.
plan.goldenHour: West Bluff Overlook, providing a view of the East Bluff illuminated by the setting sun; verify seasonal sunset timing.
